SpendLimit.description: The spend limit, spend and block state of one product and period. The top-level fields describe the total limit of the account; API key limits are nested in `credential_limits`.

blocked.description: The product is blocked for the whole account in this period (total limit). An API key's own block appears only in `credential_limits`. Always `false` in write responses; list the limits to read the block state.

credential_id.description: In write responses, the API key the write was about; `null` for the total limit. Always `null` in list entries, which describe the total limit.

credential_limits.description: List responses only. One item per API key limit of the product and period, sorted by `credential_id`, plus every API key that is still blocked. `[]` when there are none.

get.description: Returns one entry per product and period you can set a limit on, with the limit, the spend so far in the period and whether the product is blocked. An entry without a limit is still listed (`limit: null`). When the spend cannot be read, the entry is returned with `spend_usd: null` and `spend_error` set. The list is not paginated. Each entry also lists the API key limits of its product and period in `credential_limits`, with each key's spend and block. Each API key limit can be at most the total limit; together they may add up to more than it.

post.description: Sets a limit for a product and period that has none. Send exactly one of `amount` and `unlimited: true`. The period's spend is checked at once: if it is already above the new limit, the product is blocked immediately (`evaluation.blocked_now`). Returns 409 when a limit already exists for the product and period; update it instead. With `credential_id`, the limit applies to that API key only: it needs an `amount`, and the period's API key limits cannot add up to more than the total limit when the total has an amount.

delete.description: Removes the limit for the product and period. For `inference`, which has no default limit, the product becomes unlimited for the period and the period's block is lifted (`evaluation.released`). The response carries `limit: null` and the `effective_limit_usd` that applies after the removal. Returns 404 when no limit is set. With the `credential_id` query parameter, the request removes that API key's limit for the period and lifts the key's block in that period at once. A block under the key's limit in the other period stays (`evaluation.still_blocked_other_period`). Removing the total limit leaves the API key limits in place.

patch.description: Replaces the value of the existing limit for the product and period. Send exactly one of `amount` and `unlimited: true`. The period's spend is checked at once: raising the limit above the spend lifts the period's block (`evaluation.released`), and lowering it below the spend blocks the product (`evaluation.blocked_now`). Returns 404 when no limit is set; create it instead. With the `credential_id` query parameter, the request changes that API key's limit; it needs an `amount`, and it can be at most the period's total limit. Lowering the total limit below the period's highest API key limit is refused.
